Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 99, verses 1–6:

Meccan, and it has one hundred and forty-nine letters, thirty-five words, and eight verses.

Ya'qub ibn Ahmad ibn al-Sahmi al-'Aruzi informed us in Darb al-Hajib, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Uthmani informed us, saying: Abu al-Qasim al-Ta'i related to us, saying: My father related to me, saying: 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida related to me, saying: My father Musa ibn Ja'far related to me, saying: My father Ja'far ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: My father Muhammad ibn 'Ali related to me, saying: My father 'Ali ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: My father al-Husayn ibn 'Ali related to me, saying: My father 'Ali ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Idha Zulzilat four times, it is as if he has recited the whole Qur'an" [224] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/146.]].

And Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan related to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Hujr related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, saying: al-Yaman ibn al-Mughira related to us, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Idha Zulzilat equals half the Qur'an, Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad [[Surat al-Ikhlas: 1.]] equals a third of the Qur'an, and Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun [[Surat al-Kafirun: 1.]] equals a quarter of the Qur'an" [225] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 1/584.]].

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿Idha zulzilat al-ardu zilzalaha﴾ — "When the earth is shaken with its (final) shaking": Idha zulzilat means it is moved with a violent movement at the establishment of the Hour; zilzalaha means its shaking that moves it. The reading of the majority is with a kasra on the zay.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: al-Baqarji related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Yasin al-Baghdadi related to us, saying: Jamil ibn al-Hasan related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Musa, companion of al-Lu'lu', related to us, saying: I heard 'Asim al-Jahdari reading: Idha zulzilat al-ardu zalzalaha, with the zay fathah. It is also a verbal noun, like al-waswas, al-qalqal and al-jarjar. It is said: the kasra is the verbal noun and the fathah is the noun.

﴿Wa akhrajat al-ardu athqalaha﴾ — "And the earth brings forth its burdens": its dead and its treasures, so it throws them out upon its surface.

﴿Wa qala al-insanu ma laha﴾ — "And man says: What is wrong with it?" It is said that there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the verse, its meaning being: ﴿Yawma'idhin tuhaddithu akhbaraha﴾ — "On that Day it will relate its news," ﴿fa-yaqulu al-insanu: ma laha﴾ — "so man will say: What is wrong with it?"

The exegetes said: The earth will report what was done upon it, of good or evil. It will say to the believer on the Day of Resurrection: "You strove upon me, fasted, prayed, exerted yourself and obeyed your Lord," so the believer rejoices at that. And it will say to the disbeliever: "You associated partners (with Allah) upon me, committed adultery, [stole] and drank wine," so he will be rebuked before the assembly, and his limbs and the angels will bear witness against him, along with Allah's knowledge of him, until he wishes that he had been driven to the Fire because of the disgrace he sees.

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abdus al-Muzakki related to us by dictation, saying: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Hamdawayh ibn Sahl al-Marwazi informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Hammad al-Amuli related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam related to us, saying: Rushd ibn Sa'd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Salma related to us, from Abu Hazim, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the earth will report on the Day of Resurrection every deed done upon its surface." He said: And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: "Idha zulzilat al-ardu zilzalaha," until he reached "Yawma'idhin tuhaddithu akhbaraha," and said: "Do you know what its news is? When the Day of Resurrection comes, it will report every deed done upon its surface" [226] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/380, with slight variation.]].

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Mutarrif al-Jarrahi related to us, saying: Abu 'Isa 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah al-Anbari related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Khalid ibn Yazid al-'Umari related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from Yahya ibn Sulaym Abi Balj, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayra, that the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned this verse: "Yawma'idhin tuhaddithu akhbaraha," and said: "Do you know what its news is?" He said: Allah and His Messenger know best.

He (ﷺ) said: "Its news is that it will bear witness against every servant and every maidservant for what was done upon its surface. It will say: 'He did such and such upon my back, or he carried such and such upon my back on such and such a day for such and such.' This is its news" [227] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/41.]].

In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: Yawma'idhin tubbi akhbaraha ("on that Day it will give its news").

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: al-Mutarrifi informed us, saying: Bishr ibn Mutar related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'sa'a, from his father, who was an orphan in the care of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: Abu Sa'id said to me, meaning: "O my son, when you are in the deserts, raise your voice with the adhan, for I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: 'No jinn, nor human, nor stone hears it without bearing witness for him'" [228] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/6, with variation; Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/419, without variation.]].

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Amir al-Samarqandi related to us, saying: Ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Hamid related to us, from Ibrahim, from his father, who said: I saw Abu Umayya pray the obligatory prayer in the Sacred Mosque, then he advanced and began to pray here and there. When he finished, I said: "O Abu Umayya, what is this that I saw you doing?" He said: "I recited this verse: 'Yawma'idhin tuhaddithu akhbaraha,' so I wished that it would bear witness for me on the Day of Resurrection."

﴿Bi-anna rabbaka awha laha﴾ — "Because your Lord has inspired it": that is, He commanded it to speak and permitted it to do so. Al-'Ajjaj, describing the earth, said:

"He inspired it to settle, so it settled, and fastened it with the firm mountains."

That is, He commanded it to stay still.

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Qurazi and Ibn Zayd said: awha ilaiha ("He inspired to it"). The meaning of the verse is: Allah inspires to it.

﴿Yawma'idhin yasduru al-nasu ashtatan﴾ — "On that Day people will depart in scattered groups" from the place of reckoning, ashtatan meaning dispersed. ﴿Fa-man ya'mal mithqala dharratin khayran yarah. Wa man ya'mal mithqala dharratin sharran yarah﴾ — "So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it." Those who take the right side go to Paradise, and those who take the left side go to the Fire. ﴿Liyurau a'malahum﴾ — "that they may be shown their deeds." It is said: in this verse there is inversion, its meaning being: ﴿Yawma'idhin tuhaddithu akhbaraha﴾ ... ﴿bi-anna rabbaka awha laha﴾ ... ﴿Yawma'idhin yasduru al-nasu ashtatan!﴾ The reading of the majority is liyurau with a damma on the ya'.

Al-Hasan and al-A'raj read it with a fathah on the ya', and this is related from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 99, verses 7–8:

﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it,﴾ i.e., will see its reward; ﴿and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: No believer or disbeliever does any good or evil in this world except that Allah shows it to him. As for the believer, he sees his good deeds and his bad deeds; He forgives him his bad deeds and rewards him for his good deeds. As for the disbeliever, his good deeds are returned to him and He punishes him for his bad deeds.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said regarding this verse: ﴿Whoever does an atom's weight of good﴾ — this refers to a disbeliever who sees the reward of it in himself, his family, his wealth and his children until he leaves this world, and he has no good with Allah. ﴿And whoever does an atom's weight of evil﴾ — this refers to a believer who sees its punishment in this world in himself, his family, his wealth and his children until he leaves this world, and he has no evil with Allah.

The evidence for this interpretation is what:

'Aqil informed us that Abu al-Faraj informed them, on the authority of Ibn Jarir, who said: Abu al-Khattab al-Jinai related to me, who said: al-Haytham ibn al-Rabi' related to us, who said: Simak ibn 'Atiyya related to us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Abu Qilaba, on the authority of Anas, who said: Abu Bakr was eating with the Prophet (peace be upon him), and this verse was revealed: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾ Abu Bakr - may Allah be pleased with him - raised his hand and said:

"O Messenger of Allah, shall I be recompensed for what I have done of an atom's weight of evil?" He said: "O Abu Bakr, what you have seen in this world of what you dislike is from the atoms' weights of evil, and Allah will store up for you atoms' weights of good [[In the original: "atoms' weights of good."]] until you meet Him on the Day of Resurrection."
[229] [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/577.]]

Also from him, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Hayy ibn 'Abd Allah related to me, on the authority of Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Jili, on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, that he said:

"Surah al-Zalzalah was revealed while Abu Bakr al-Siddiq - may Allah be pleased with him - was sitting, and he wept when it was revealed. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'What makes you weep, O Abu Bakr?' He said: 'This surah has made me weep.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'By Allah, if you did not err or sin, and Allah forgave you, He would create a people who err and sin, and He would forgive them.'"
[230] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/141, with slight variation.]]

The common reading is yarahu with a fatha on the ya' in both places. Khalid ibn Nashit and 'Asim al-Jahdari read it with a damma on both ya's, based on the words li-yuraw (﴿that they may be shown﴾).

Muqatil said: This verse was revealed concerning two men. When the verse ﴿and they give food, despite their love for it﴾ [Surah al-Insan 76:8] was revealed, one of them would have a beggar come to him, and he would consider it too little to give him a date, a morsel of bread, a nut, or the like, and would say: "This is nothing; we are rewarded only for what we give, and we love it." Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They give food despite their love for it﴾, so whoever loves this for us, rejecting it is forgiveness. The other would belittle small sins—lies, backbiting, a glance, and the like—and would say: "Nothing of this is upon me; Allah the Exalted has promised the Fire only for the major sins, and there is no sin in this." So Allah the Exalted revealed this to encourage them to give even a little good, for it will soon grow, and to warn them against small sins, for they will soon grow large. The small sin in the eyes of its doer on the Day of Resurrection is greater than the mountains, and all of his good deeds are less in his eyes than anything. So He said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾

Tha'lab was asked about the dharra (atom). He said: "A hundred of them are the weight of a grain, and the dharra is one of them." Yazid ibn [Marwan] said: "It is said that the dharra has no weight; and the meaning of mithqal is weight, and it is a form (mif'al) from heaviness (thiql)." Ibn Mas'ud said: "The most precise verse in the Qur'an is ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾" The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to call it "the all-encompassing, unique [verse]."
[231] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 3/79.]]

Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas gave two dates in charity, and the beggar withdrew his hand. Sa'd said: "Woe to you! May Allah accept from us the weight of an atom and a mustard seed; how many weights of such things there are in this!"

'Umar ibn al-Khattab and 'A'isha gave in charity a grape, and both said: "In it are many weights of atoms."

Al-Muttalib [ibn 'Abd Allah, on the authority of 'A'isha] narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited in a gathering in which a Bedouin was sitting. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾" The Bedouin said: "O Messenger of Allah, an atom's weight?" He said: "Yes." The Bedouin said: "O Messenger of Allah, an atom's weight?" He said: "Yes." The Bedouin said: "Woe to us then!" and he got up while saying it. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Faith has entered the heart of the Bedouin."
[232] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/152 and al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/381.]]

'Abd Allah ibn Hatib informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Amir al-Samarqandi informed us, who said: 'Umar ibn Yahya related to us, who said: 'Abd ibn Humayd related to us, on the authority of Wahb ibn Jarir, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard al-Hasan say: "Sa'sa'a, the paternal uncle of al-Farazdaq, came to the Prophet (peace be upon him). When he heard ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾, he said: 'That is enough for me; I do not mind, and I do not want to hear any other part of the Qur'an than this.'"
[233] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/153 and Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/420.]]

al-Rabi' ibn Subayh said: A man passed by al-Hasan while he was reciting this surah. When he reached its end, the man said: "That is enough for me; I have completed the admonition." Al-Hasan said: "Indeed the man has understood (faqiha)."
[234]

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Mufassir recited to us. He said: Abu al-Fadl Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdun al-Faqih recited to me, who said: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Hawwari recited to me in Wasit:

Indeed, whoever transgresses and earns sin—
the weight of an atom he will see it.

And he will be repaid for his evil deed with evil,
and for a good deed, He also repays him with good.

Thus is the saying of my Lord, blessed is He,
in "When the earth is shaken," exalted is His praise.
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/152.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 99, verses 7–8:

﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it,﴾ i.e., will see its reward; ﴿and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: No believer or disbeliever does any good or evil in this world except that Allah shows it to him. As for the believer, he sees his good deeds and his bad deeds; He forgives him his bad deeds and rewards him for his good deeds. As for the disbeliever, his good deeds are returned to him and He punishes him for his bad deeds.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said regarding this verse: ﴿Whoever does an atom's weight of good﴾ — this refers to a disbeliever who sees the reward of it in himself, his family, his wealth and his children until he leaves this world, and he has no good with Allah. ﴿And whoever does an atom's weight of evil﴾ — this refers to a believer who sees its punishment in this world in himself, his family, his wealth and his children until he leaves this world, and he has no evil with Allah.

The evidence for this interpretation is what:

'Aqil informed us that Abu al-Faraj informed them, on the authority of Ibn Jarir, who said: Abu al-Khattab al-Jinai related to me, who said: al-Haytham ibn al-Rabi' related to us, who said: Simak ibn 'Atiyya related to us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Abu Qilaba, on the authority of Anas, who said: Abu Bakr was eating with the Prophet (peace be upon him), and this verse was revealed: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾ Abu Bakr - may Allah be pleased with him - raised his hand and said:

"O Messenger of Allah, shall I be recompensed for what I have done of an atom's weight of evil?" He said: "O Abu Bakr, what you have seen in this world of what you dislike is from the atoms' weights of evil, and Allah will store up for you atoms' weights of good [[In the original: "atoms' weights of good."]] until you meet Him on the Day of Resurrection."
[229] [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/577.]]

Also from him, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Hayy ibn 'Abd Allah related to me, on the authority of Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Jili, on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, that he said:

"Surah al-Zalzalah was revealed while Abu Bakr al-Siddiq - may Allah be pleased with him - was sitting, and he wept when it was revealed. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'What makes you weep, O Abu Bakr?' He said: 'This surah has made me weep.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'By Allah, if you did not err or sin, and Allah forgave you, He would create a people who err and sin, and He would forgive them.'"
[230] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/141, with slight variation.]]

The common reading is yarahu with a fatha on the ya' in both places. Khalid ibn Nashit and 'Asim al-Jahdari read it with a damma on both ya's, based on the words li-yuraw (﴿that they may be shown﴾).

Muqatil said: This verse was revealed concerning two men. When the verse ﴿and they give food, despite their love for it﴾ [Surah al-Insan 76:8] was revealed, one of them would have a beggar come to him, and he would consider it too little to give him a date, a morsel of bread, a nut, or the like, and would say: "This is nothing; we are rewarded only for what we give, and we love it." Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They give food despite their love for it﴾, so whoever loves this for us, rejecting it is forgiveness. The other would belittle small sins—lies, backbiting, a glance, and the like—and would say: "Nothing of this is upon me; Allah the Exalted has promised the Fire only for the major sins, and there is no sin in this." So Allah the Exalted revealed this to encourage them to give even a little good, for it will soon grow, and to warn them against small sins, for they will soon grow large. The small sin in the eyes of its doer on the Day of Resurrection is greater than the mountains, and all of his good deeds are less in his eyes than anything.
